basis: Panniculitis destroys subcutaneous fat; lipoatrophy is obligate. Localized fat loss does not establish a metabolic disorder.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation and abnormal immunoglobulins do not establish autoimmunity or another qualifying immune mechanism; ANA positivity is only occasional.

basis: Monocytic blood and marrow malignancy; direct leukemic gingival infiltration occurs in roughly 30-60%. Skin and CNS infiltration are minority manifestations.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: direct gingival leukemic infiltration occurs in approximately 30-60% of acute monocytic leukemia; gums belong to this axis.

basis: Distal, ocular and pharyngeal myopathy define disease; direct tongue weakness affects oral function in 30-79%. Hearing loss is occasional; aspiration pneumonia is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: tongue muscle weakness occurs in 30-79% and directly impairs oral function; this adds evidence beyond pharyngeal dysphagia alone.

basis: Eye-movement dysfunction defines this umbrella. Common strabismus and muscular forms do not require cranial nerve or CNS disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: the cranial-neuropathy parent is overly broad for children including strabismus and muscular disorders; neural damage is not shared by most patients.

basis: Congenital O-mannosylation disorder with muscular dystrophy and brain malformations; defining eye malformations (retinal dysplasia 2/2) occupy involved because primary is capped at three.

decisions.ocular: involved: structural eye malformations are defining; retinal dysplasia occurs in 2/2 annotated patients. The three-primary cap requires placement here.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the established congenital O-mannosylation defect is an inborn glycosylation disorder, supported by the supplied ancestry rather than the gene alone.

basis: Organism-defined bacterial infection; most human cases (>50%) involve direct cutaneous infection as erysipeloid. Endocarditis is uncommon.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: localized cutaneous erysipeloid accounts for most human infections (>50%); this genus-wide concept is defined by its pathogen rather than a required skin location.

basis: Intrinsic cytopenias, marrow failure and cerebellar ataxia characterize the defined spectrum. Myeloid neoplasm susceptibility adds no further organ.

decisions.neurologic: primary: ataxia is an explicitly defining clinical component of the supplied spectrum, rather than an organ inferred from the gene or future cancer risk.

basis: Renal ciliopathy with defining Joubert-spectrum cerebellar vermis hypoplasia in the supplied classification. Retinal degeneration is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: the supplied Joubert syndrome parent and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia support a defining CNS malformation; this is not inferred from ZNF423 alone.

basis: Direct skin lesions ~60-80%, lung involvement ~30-60%, and marrow infiltration with cytopenias >30%; hepatic involvement (~30-50%) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: disseminated infection commonly infiltrates marrow with impaired blood-cell production (>30%); isolated anemia alone would not suffice.
decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic involvement (~30-50%) can qualify, but skin, pulmonary and marrow injury receive priority under the four-axis cap.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: direct pulmonary infection with infiltrates occurs in approximately 30-60%; this exceeds the threshold independently of respiratory symptoms alone.

basis: Reflux-associated dystonic posturing defines the syndrome. Anemia is frequent (30-79%) but reflects secondary bleeding or iron deficiency rather than direct blood or marrow disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: despite the 30-79% annotation, bleeding-related or iron-deficiency anemia is a secondary, separately diagnosed condition rather than direct hematologic damage.
